issues.location: Executive Summary & Understanding (Business & Financial Impact, Operational Challenges)
issues.description: The proposal hallucinates specific financial and operational metrics not present in the Client Matrix, including "$85M in annual revenue", "growing 40% in 2024", "40 dispatchers", and "~600 contracted drivers". Presenting fabricated business metrics to a client is a critical risk that would severely damage the firm's credibility.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove all fabricated metrics. Replace them with qualitative descriptions supported by the matrix (e.g., "following recent acquisitions") and strictly use only the provided numbers ($1.4M working capital, $320k savings, avoiding 4 additional dispatchers).

issues.description: The proposal invents specific technologies and third-party systems not mentioned in the matrix, specifically "NetSuite", "Rails 5", and "React Native". Guessing the client's tech stack and accounting software could embarrass the firm if incorrect.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace "NetSuite" with "accounting/finance system", "Rails 5" with "legacy dispatch system", and "React Native" with "mobile application".

issues.description: The proposal hallucinates a stakeholder name and title ("Head of Compliance Rajiv Mehta") that does not exist in the Client Matrix.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the fabricated name and refer generically to "the compliance team" or "relevant compliance stakeholders."

issues.description: The proposal completely omits a high-confidence fact from the matrix: previous internal attempts to fix the workflow issues have failed twice. Omitting this misses a key opportunity to justify the external engagement and address a major historical risk.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a bullet point in the Technical Environment section acknowledging the two previous failed internal attempts, and briefly note in the Approach section how the proposed methodology mitigates the risk of a third failure.

risks: The Proposal Agent is heavily hallucinating specific client details (financial metrics, tech stack, personnel) to fill in narrative gaps. This poses a severe risk to the firm's credibility if not strictly controlled.

By failing to acknowledge past internal project failures, the proposal misses an opportunity to build trust and explain why an external consultancy is necessary to succeed where internal teams could not.
